ic_name: NFC / ISO 14443 (NXP AN10833 MIFARE family — subset)

protocol_overview.type: Contactless inductively-coupled half-duplex command-response protocol over a 13.56 MHz RF carrier. PCD (reader) is the master and always initiates a transaction; PICC (card) is the slave and only transmits when addressed. Three protocol layers: Layer 2 (ISO 14443-2) defines modulation/coding; Layer 3 (ISO 14443-3) defines anti-collision and selection; Layer 4 (ISO 14443-4) defines the T=CL Block Transmission Protocol.
protocol_overview.duplex: half-duplex (PCD modulates carrier amplitude; PICC modulates load on the carrier — never simultaneous)
protocol_overview.pcd_role: Generates 13.56 MHz RF field; powers the PICC by inductive coupling; initiates every transaction; encodes PCD→PICC bits as Modified Miller (Type A, 100% ASK) or NRZ (Type B, 10% ASK).
protocol_overview.picc_role: Field-powered; responds only when polled; encodes PICC→PCD bits as Manchester (Type A) or BPSK (Type B) load modulation on the 847.5 kHz subcarrier.

functional_requirements.text: The air interface shall use a single 13.56 MHz RF carrier per ISO/IEC 14443-2. Operating range shall be 0-100 mm from the PCD antenna with proximity (≤ 10 cm) as the typical functional envelope.
Type A PCD→PICC shall use 100% ASK Modified Miller coding at one of 106 / 212 / 424 / 848 kbps (fc/128, fc/64, fc/32, fc/16). 106 kbps shall be the initial / mandatory rate.
Type A PICC→PCD shall use Manchester coding via load modulation of an 847.5 kHz subcarrier (fc/16) on the 13.56 MHz carrier.
Type B PCD→PICC shall use 10% ASK NRZ-L coding at 106 / 212 / 424 / 848 kbps. PICC→PCD shall use BPSK of the 847.5 kHz subcarrier.
A PCD shall initiate Layer-3 polling using REQA (0x26, 7-bit short frame) or WUPA (0x52, 7-bit short frame). All PICCs in the IDLE / HALT state respectively shall reply with ATQA.

Every Type A PICC shall reply to REQA / WUPA with a 16-bit ATQA (transmitted LSB-first, two bytes) encoding bit-frame anti-collision support bitmap and UID size (00 = single 4 B, 01 = double 7 B, 10 = triple 10 B; 11 = RFU).

PCDs shall perform bit-frame anti-collision per ISO/IEC 14443-3 §6.4.3 using SELECT cascade levels CL1 (0x93), CL2 (0x95), CL3 (0x97). At each level the PCD shall transmit the cascade-level SEL byte + NVB byte + (UID-CLn[4:0]) + (BCC). The PICC shall respond with the remaining UID-CLn bits.
Each Cascade-Level block shall be protected by a BCC (Block Check Character) = UID-CLn[0] XOR UID-CLn[1] XOR UID-CLn[2] XOR UID-CLn[3].
UID lengths shall be 4 bytes (single, single CL), 7 bytes (double, CL1 + CL2 with Cascade Tag 0x88 at UID-CL1[0]), or 10 bytes (triple, CL1 + CL2 + CL3 each preceded by 0x88).
Cascade Tag CT = 0x88 (Type A) shall mark a UID block that is not yet complete; CT shall appear as UID-CLn[0] for all non-final cascade levels.

After the PCD transmits a complete SELECT for the final cascade level, the PICC shall return a 1-byte SAK (Select Acknowledge) + CRC_A. SAK bit 3 = 1 means UID not complete (Cascade Tag follows); SAK bit 6 = 1 means PICC supports ISO/IEC 14443-4 (T=CL).
UID byte 0 shall be the IC Manufacturer Byte per ISO/IEC 7816-6: 0x04 = NXP, 0x05 = Infineon, 0x07 = STMicroelectronics, 0x08 = Random ID (UID0 = 0x08, UID1..UID3 random).
A PICC shall transition to HALT state on receipt of HLTA (0x50 0x00 + CRC_A); the PCD shall use WUPA (0x52) instead of REQA (0x26) to re-poll HALT-state PICCs.
When SAK indicates ISO/IEC 14443-4 support (bit 6 = 1), the PCD may activate Layer 4 by transmitting RATS (0xE0 + Param byte = FSDI<<4 | CID) and the PICC shall reply with ATS (Answer To Select).

ATS shall be a length-prefixed structure: TL (length) + T0 (interface bytes present + FSCI) + optional TA(1) (DS/DR bit rate support bitmap) / TB(1) (FWI / SFGI guard times) / TC(1) (NAD / CID support) + historical bytes. FSCI shall encode the maximum frame size the PICC accepts in bytes (16..256).

Layer 4 (T=CL Block Transmission Protocol) shall use three block types: I-Block (information / chained APDU), R-Block (acknowledgement / NAK), S-Block (DESELECT or WTX wait-time-extension). PCB (Protocol Control Byte) is the first byte of each block.
Frames longer than the short-frame size shall be protected by CRC_A = CRC-16/X-25-style with poly 0x8408 (reflected 0x1021), initial value 0x6363, no final XOR, transmitted LSB-first.
Type B frames shall use CRC_B = CRC-16/X-25 with poly 0x1021 (reflected to 0x8408), initial value 0xFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFF, transmitted LSB-first.
A PICC may use a Random ID (RID) for privacy: UID0 = 0x08 fixed, UID1..UID3 are randomized at each Power-on Reset.

For exact identification beyond ATQA/SAK, the PCD should issue GetVersion (0x60) on PICCs that advertise the command (MIFARE Ultralight EV1, MIFARE Plus EV1/EV2, MIFARE DESFire EV2/EV3, MIFARE DESFire Light). Byte 2 of the response (HW/Product Type) deterministically identifies the family.

configurations.name: Type A 106 kbps + ISO 14443-3 only
configurations.description: MIFARE Classic / Ultralight / NTAG21x default. SAK bit 6 = 0. Native (non-T=CL) protocol above Layer 3.

configurations.name: Type A 106 kbps + ISO 14443-4 T=CL
configurations.description: MIFARE DESFire / DESFire Light / MIFARE Plus SL2/SL3 / JCOP. SAK bit 6 = 1. T=CL carries APDU above.

configurations.name: Type A higher rates (212/424/848 kbps)
configurations.description: Negotiated by PPS (Protocol and Parameter Selection) after ATS for ISO 14443-4 PICCs.

configurations.name: Type B + ISO 14443-4 T=CL
configurations.description: ATQB returns 12 bytes (PUPI 4 B + Application Data 4 B + Protocol Info 4 B); ATTRIB selects; Layer 4 same as Type A.

configurations.name: Random ID (RID) privacy mode
configurations.description: PICC randomises UID1..UID3; UID0 = 0x08. Used by MIFARE DESFire EV2/EV3 in Random-ID configuration and by NFC-A peer devices.

error_response_conditions: Bit collision during anti-collision — PCD detects the collision bit-position from the Manchester subcarrier and re-transmits SELECT with NVB extended to the collision bit + 1. Resolution proceeds until exactly one PICC remains.
CRC_A / CRC_B mismatch — PICC silently ignores the malformed frame; PCD detects via response timeout and may retry (typically up to 3 retries).
Parity error on Type A — each byte is followed by one odd-parity bit; PICC drops a frame on parity error and does not respond.
Frame size violation — PCD shall not transmit an I-Block exceeding the PICC's FSCI-advertised size; PICC shall not transmit a response exceeding the PCD's FSDI.
PICC moves to HALT after HLTA (0x50 0x00 + CRC_A); subsequent REQA shall not wake it (WUPA required).
Loss of carrier / removal from field — PICC loses VCC and returns to IDLE on re-entry; all session state (CID, FSCI negotiation, T=CL block number) is lost.
WTX (Wait Time Extension) requested by PICC via S-Block when an internal operation requires longer than the negotiated FWT (Frame Waiting Time).
Block-number desynchronisation — T=CL uses a 1-bit alternating block number; mismatch indicates lost block and triggers retransmission via R(NAK).
compliance_requirements: PCD shall maintain Hmin operating field strength of 1.5 A/m and Hmax of 7.5 A/m at the operating volume per ISO 14443-2 (Class 1/2/3/4 antenna geometry classes).
PCD shall use 100% ASK + Modified Miller for Type A and 10% ASK + NRZ-L for Type B PCD→PICC paths.
PICC shall power up, decode REQA, and respond with ATQA within fdt_listen ≤ 86.43 μs (the Frame Delay Time-listen for short-frame mandated anti-collision).
PCD shall wait at least fdt_poll ≥ 1172 / fc ≈ 86.43 μs after the end of the PICC response before transmitting again.
PICC initial response shall always be at 106 kbps; higher rates require explicit PPS negotiation after RATS.
PCD shall implement the bit-frame anti-collision loop until exactly one PICC is selected; multiple PICCs in field require iteration.
PCD shall validate SAK bit 6 before issuing RATS — issuing RATS to a non-14443-4 PICC is a violation and PICC behavior is undefined.
Application-layer commands above Layer 4 shall be wrapped as APDUs in I-Block payload per the appropriate MIFARE / NFC Forum / ISO 7816-4 specification.
